goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
goldens.reasoning: G1 is about a compile error: a call with the required UserModel argument missing in UsernameForm. C1 says both call sites pass context.getUser(), so it does not flag a missing parameter.

goldens.comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
goldens.reasoning: C1 explains that the user != null requirement stops fillContextForm from running on the initial login page, which breaks conditional passkeys. This is the same issue as G2.

candidates: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:161 - Passkeys are enabled only when a user is already set, which is the reverse of the intended condition. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` ends with `&& user != null`. The old code filled the WebAuthn form when `context.getUser() == null`, which is a normal first login. Both new call sites now pass `context.getUser()`. On a fresh login the user is null, so `fillContextForm` is never called and the conditional-UI passkey form is missing. The same happens in `challenge(...)` after a bad password when the user was cleared. Only the re-authentication case, where the user is already set, gets passkeys. The tests in this PR expect `//form[@id='webauth']` on the initial login page, so they would fail. Allow a null user: `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. If re-authentication needs extra conditions, apply them only when the user is non-null.
